transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

If the motor is running but the drum isn't turning, the most likely cause is that the drive belt has snapped or slipped off. This is a common failure and usually means the belt needs replacing. To confirm this, please unplug the dryer first. With the drum empty, try to turn it by hand. If it spins around very easily with no resistance at all (like an empty wheel), that suggests the belt has broken or come off the pulley. If it feels stiff or stuck, something else may be jammed inside. Please let me know what you feel when turning it by hand.
ok unplugged it and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy almost no resistance at all

This is a very common failure on Hotpoint dryers and means the belt needs replacing. To get you the right part, I need the model number. It’s usually on a sticker inside the door opening or on the back of the machine. What does it say?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
the sticker is worn but i can see it starts TVHM8 the rest has rubbed off. also theres a black rubbery strip lying at the bottom when i look through the filter slot with a torch

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
That suggests it: the drive belt has snapped or slipped off. The 'spins very easily' feeling and seeing that black rubber strip are classic signs of a broken belt on Hotpoint dryers. Because I cannot verify your exact model number (TVHM8 is only a partial prefix), I cannot guarantee part compatibility from my side. You should contact the manufacturer’s spares service or an authorised engineer with the full serial number (usually found on the door rim or back panel) to order the correct belt and have it fitted, as this requires opening the machine casing.
i can take the back panel off with a screwdriver if you tell me how, id rather fit the belt myself. how do i find the right belt without the full model number

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
To find the correct belt without the full model number, look for a white sticker on the door rim (the frame that holds the glass) or on the back of the machine; it will have a 'Model' and a 'PNC' (Part Number Code). The PNC is an 8-digit number starting with zeros (e.g.If you cannot find a PNC or feel unsure about reassembling the casing safely, please call an engineer.
ok the sticker on the door rim is worn so i only have TVHM8. the assistants last message got cut off tho, whats the PNC thing and how do i take the back panel off

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
The PNC (Part Number Code) is an 8-digit code on the rating sticker that identifies the exact configuration of your machine, which is essential because 'TVHM8' covers many different internal variations. Regarding the repair: while it is possible to access the belt by removing the rear panel on some models (usually held by screws around the perimeter), this varies significantly between Hotpoint variants. Given the risk of buying the wrong part and the complexity of accessing the drive system without a confirmed manual, I strongly recommend calling an engineer or using the manufacturer's official repair service.
